hooks.text: A human sprint could launch you straight into orbit around Mars.
Can you run fast enough to escape a moon's gravity?
This Martian moon is so small that a human can outrun its gravity.

title: How to Launch into Mars Orbit by Running
description: Discover Deimos, the tiny Martian moon where the gravity is so weak that a fast human runner can reach escape velocity.

beats.text: A human sprint could launch you straight into orbit around Mars.
beats.visual: Global full-disk view of Deimos captured by the Emirates Mars Mission, 2023

beats.text: In August 1877, astronomer Asaph Hall was ready to give up his search for Martian moons.
beats.visual: Historical portrait of astronomer Asaph Hall, circa 1880

beats.text: His wife, Angeline Stickney, urged him to continue his search at the US Naval Observatory.
beats.visual: Portrait photograph of Chloe Angeline Stickney Hall

beats.text: Hall discovered Deimos, a smooth, dusty moon twelve kilometers wide that acts like a cosmic springboard.
beats.visual: Deimos high-resolution color composite from the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter HiRISE, 2009

beats.text: Its surface gravity is so weak that its escape velocity is only 13 miles per hour.
beats.visual: Solar transit of Deimos across the Sun imaged by the Opportunity rover, 2004

beats.text: That is slower than a fast human runner, meaning a simple sprint overcomes the moon’s entire gravity.
beats.visual: Artist illustration of an astronaut jumping high off a small asteroid surface

beats.text: While its sister moon Phobos is spiraling toward Mars, Deimos is slowly drifting away into space.
beats.visual: Artist's illustration of Mars with Phobos and Deimos in orbit

beats.text: On Deimos, a simple sprint is enough to reach escape velocity.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of the smooth regolith on the surface of Deimos

better_than_last: Applied the loop-back strategy by ending with a complete sentence that sets up the hook's premise for a seamless rewatch.
